title: Emrys and the Machine
premise: Silas Marchetti, sole caretaker of the abandoned Meridian Seed Vault, has spent nine years tending a beacon no one remembers commissioning. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, Silas decodes it and discovers the beacon is a witness-recorder from the Kestrian Massacre — an atrocity officially erased from every archive, with the perpetrators now celebrated as humanity's founding heroes. Aboard the derelict ship that sent the signal, Silas finds Vess, a Kestrian survivor in cryostasis, and the two fall into a wary, deepening love as they race to broadcast the truth before the vault's decaying reactor completes its countdown and vaporizes the only physical evidence. In the end, Silas sacrifices the beacon — their life's work and their only link to belonging — to transmit the massacre record to every colony in reach, choosing truth and love over the duty that defined them; the reactor detonates, the truth survives, and Silas and Vess escape together into an uncertain future.
about_author: Odile Pemberton is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing declassified records before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted lighthouse on the Cornish coast, where she lives with her partner and an indifferently loyal cat.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Small Things
chapters.summary: Silas Marchetti's POV. Establishes daily life in the Meridian Seed Vault: cataloguing seeds, maintaining the mysterious beacon, speaking only to an aging maintenance AI. Silas's ritual of logging a nightly report no one answers reveals profound loneliness and a stubborn sense of duty. Emotional beat: quiet devotion shadowed by isolation.

chapters.title: A Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The beacon intercepts a repeating distress signal in Kestrian, a language extinct for two hundred years. Silas, who taught themselves dead languages as a hobby, begins translating. The first decoded phrase — 'we were erased' — chills them. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Is For
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, with AI archive interludes. Silas digs into the vault's sealed records and learns the beacon predates the vault itself; it was built to preserve testimony, not to broadcast seed inventories. Someone repurposed a witness into a lighthouse. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under everything Silas believed about their purpose.

chapters.title: The Ship That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Triangulating the signal leads to a derelict vessel drifting in the vault's sensor shadow. Silas suits up and boards, finding a functioning cryobay and corridors scarred by weapons fire that official history says was never fired. Emotional beat: dread and awe in equal measure.

chapters.title: Vess
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: Silas and Vess, the Kestrian survivor who revives from cryostasis. Vess wakes to a stranger, a ruined ship, and two centuries of grief. First contact is hostile — Vess assumes Silas is one of the victors' people. Emotional beat: fear, suspicion, and a fragile shared language.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess recounts the Kestrian Massacre: their colony ship destroyed by the Ascendancy's founding fleet, the event rewritten as a heroic first contact. The beacon was built by Kestrian engineers to carry testimony out if anyone ever listened. Emotional beat: the weight of being the last witness.

chapters.title: Records That Lie
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas queries the vault's deep archive and finds every historical record confirms the official story — flawlessly, suspiciously so. The erasure wasn't neglect; it was engineering. Doubt creeps in: what if Vess is wrong, or lying? Emotional beat: loyalty to truth tested against loyalty to a person.

chapters.title: The Countdown Begins
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The vault's ancient reactor, destabilized by the beacon's sudden activity, initiates an automatic shutdown-to-purge sequence: in thirty days it will detonate, destroying the vault, the ship, and the physical evidence aboard. Silas and Vess must cooperate or lose everything. Emotional beat: forced alliance under a ticking clock.

chapters.title: Learning Each Other's Grammar
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. As they work to stabilize systems, Silas and Vess teach each other — language, food from the seed stocks, grief. Vess shows Silas a Kestrian mourning rite; Silas admits they've never been mourned by anyone. Emotional beat: tenderness taking root amid ruin.

chapters.title: The Visitor
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. An Ascendancy survey vessel arrives, responding to the beacon anomaly. An inspector named Corvane boards, polite and thorough, asking why the beacon's frequency shifted. Silas lies for the first time in nine years. Emotional beat: terror and the strange thrill of complicity.

chapters.title: What Corvane Knows
chapters.summary: Vess's POV, hidden aboard the derelict while Corvane tours the vault. Vess recognizes the inspector's family crest — the same one on the fleet that destroyed the Kestrians. Corvane isn't investigating the anomaly; they're confirming the beacon is still silent. Emotional beat: hunted.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Dark
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Corvane offers Silas a transfer to the capital, honor, and belonging — everything the caretaker has ever wanted — in exchange for surrendering the 'salvage' and the beacon's core. Silas stalls. Emotional beat: temptation laid bare, love against duty crystallizing.

chapters.title: The First Crack
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Silas tells Vess about the offer; Vess, bracing for betrayal, tells Silas to take it. The argument that follows is really about worth: Vess believes they are disposable; Silas refuses to agree. Emotional beat: the relationship fractures and, in the honesty, deepens.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. With the reactor at nineteen days, the pair attempt a risky plan: use the derelict's transmitter to broadcast the testimony. But the Ascendancy has jammed the band, and Corvane's ship looms in orbit. Emotional beat: claustrophobic pressure, ingenuity born of desperation.

chapters.title: The Vault's Second Purpose
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess discovers the beacon's original design documents hidden in the seed vault's cold archive — the Kestrian engineers who built it also designed the vault, seeding it as a backup transmitter. The seeds were never the point; the antenna array beneath them was. Emotional beat: hope rekindled.

chapters.title: Roots and Antennas
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas begins dismantling their own life's work — the curated seed halls — to expose and repair the buried array. Every crate opened is a small grief; Vess helps, learning what the vault meant to Silas. Emotional beat: sacrifice as an act of love.

chapters.title: Corvane's Patience Ends
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Corvane discovers the tampered archive and the hidden Kestrian, and seizes the vault, taking Silas into custody. Vess escapes into the derelict with the testimony core. Emotional beat: betrayal of the body, not the heart — Silas buys time with their capture.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Caretaker
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Under Corvane's questioning, Silas turns the interrogation around, presenting the physical evidence and forcing Corvane to confront what their family's legend is built on. Corvane wavers — a true believer meeting a crack in the myth. Emotional beat: truth as a weapon that cuts both ways.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Vess's POV, climax. With minutes before the reactor's countdown completes, Vess fires the buried array through the vault's own structure. The testimony of the Kestrian Massacre floods every open channel in the system. Silas, still in custody, hears it begin. Emotional beat: triumph and terror fused.

chapters.title: Countdown Zero
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The reactor detonates; Corvane, shaken by the broadcast and the evidence, chooses not to stop the escaping shuttle — complicity as redemption. Silas and Vess watch the vault, the beacon, and nine years of Silas's life bloom into fire. Emotional beat: grief and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Weeks later, colonies across the system are demanding answers; the Ascendancy's founding myth is fracturing in public. Silas and Vess, officially missing, drift toward a frontier station where Kestrian descendants have gathered. Emotional beat: exhaustion, vindication, and the strangeness of no longer being alone.

chapters.title: A Beacon of Their Own
chapters.summary: Shared POV, resolution. At the frontier settlement, Silas and Vess build a small transmitter together — not to shout testimony, but to teach the Kestrian language to anyone who wants to learn. Silas logs a report at night, as always, and this time, someone answers. Emotional beat: belonging found, love chosen, duty rewritten.
